description.narrative:
The overarching goal of Diakonias country strategy for Colombia is to mobilise society for peacebuilding, making the conditions for peace a national priority. In particular, the organisation identifies the holistic implementation of existing peace accords, strengthened guarantees for the protection and safety of civil society organisations and the initiation of new peace-talks, as such prioritised conditions for peace.
To achieve this, Diakonia proposes to strengthen and to work together with local civil society organisations to generate significant changes and structural transformations in four interrelated areas or change processes, each with its own set of objectives and results indicators:
1. Strengthened capacity of civil society to exercise democratic participation, defence of human rights and active citizenship. 2. Implementation of the peace agreements, new peace-talks and national reconciliation. 3. Increased gender equality in social, economic and political structures. 4. Environmental justice and defence of the right to a healthy environment

Kärnstödet till Diakonia i Colombia syftar till att bidra till en stabil och varaktig fred i landet med ett nationellt, territoriellt och rättighetsbaserat perspektiv. Detta stöd är en fortsättning av en tidigare insats med ID 10781. De övergripande målen är följande:
1) Stärkt kapacitet hos det civila samhället att utöva demokratiskt deltagande, försvar av mänskliga rättigheter och aktivt medborgarskap. 2) Genomförande av fredsavtalet, nya fredssamtal och nationell försoning. 3) Ökad jämställdhet i sociala, ekonomiska och politiska strukturer. 4) Miljörättvisa och försvar av rätten till en hälsosam miljö.

The support to Diakonia cointains two components; a core funding to the country plan; and a project support to a civil society fund. The components aim at contributing to a stable and lasting peace in Colombia with a national, territorial, and right-based perspective. The overall objectives are the following:
1) Strengthened capacity of civil society to exercise democratic participation, defence of human rights and active citizenship. 2) Implementation of the peace agreement, new peace-talks, and national reconciliation. 3) Increased gender equality in social, economic, and political structures. 4) Environmental justice and defence of the right to a healthy environment.
This support is a continuation of previous contribution with ID-number 10781.

description.narrative:
Main results achieved in 2025:
Positioning of the feminist peace agenda and the importance of the meaningful participation of women in peace dialogues through the international advocacy carried out by the organization SISMA before the European Union and the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW).
The launch and broad media dissemination of the report EGC in Chocó: violence, power, and fear, which was shared with the governments negotiation team for sociolegal dialogues with the Gaitanista Army of Colombia (EGC), the Ombudsmans Office, and delegates from one of the larger community organization in the zone, COCOMACIA. This effort enabled the reports findings to reach a thematic audience before the InterAmerican Commission on Human Rights (IACHR), placing the rights violations of the ethnic population on the agenda of public opinion and multilateral bodies.
During 2025, 329 women victims of gender-based violence and violence within the framework of the armed conflict received legal support (107 women before the ordinary justice system and 222 women accredited before the Transitional Justice system, the JEP), and 82 women and LGBTIQ individuals received psychosocial support, including in some cases international legal representation before the IACHR and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW) Committee.
Approximately 232 people (93% of them womensocial leaders, Indigenous, Afrodescendant, rural, students, and migrants) participated in seven (7) training processes aimed at strengthening their comprehensive empowerment and the exercise of rights, in areas such as political leadership, gender and violence, the care economy, sexual and reproductive rights, and gender and intersectionality.
With the support of the Program, partner organizations implemented throughout 2025 a comprehensive communication and social awareness strategy with high impact that contributes to transforming social imaginaries, rejecting violence, promoting equality, and building citizen support for peace. At the same time, they amplified the voices of victims and positioned feminist analyses on the public agenda, helping to keep this issue a political and social priority.
The 14th edition of the National Human Rights Award consolidated its position as one of the main platforms for recognizing and raising the visibility of individuals and organizations defending human rights in Colombia. The Award expanded its territorial reach and saw broad participation from national and international actors, including the European Union and the United Nations in addition to the Embassy.
At least eight specialized reports were produced on political violence, the humanitarian crisis, and impacts on human rights defenders. These were used by the Constitutional Court, United Nations bodies, the InterAmerican Commission on Human Rights (IACHR), and international cooperation actors. Through this documentary production, partner organizations continue to serve as technical references for monitoring the human rights situation and the conditions of those who defend them.
Partner organizations achieved concrete progress through policy dialogue and direct influence on the National Protection System and the Comprehensive Public Policy of Guarantees for human rights defenders, incorporating differential approaches for women, Indigenous peoples, peasant communities, Afro descendant communities, and the LGBTIQ population.
In 2025 the Swedish Fund supported 19 organisations, covering 11 departments and reaching 9.492 people. 65% of the organisations supported had little or none experience working with international cooperation, this means that the fund is working with local organisations.
Tripartite projects of the Swedish Fund produced valuable results. The work with the Land Restitution Unit developed a participatory model for returning land to peasant collectives, which could be scaled up to 61 collective cases in different territories.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
